court: In the High Court of Madras
judges_raw: (Before M.M. Sundresh and Krishnan Ramasamy, JJ.)
case_number: C.M.P. No. 17061 of 2019 and A.S.SR. No. 46860 of 2019
judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

M.M. Sundresh, J.:— Petitioner is the first defendant in the suit filed for partition and separate possession and the suit was decreed on 01.06.2016. The present petition has been filed seeking to condone the delay of 938 days in filing the appeal on the premise that the petitioner was suffering from severe diabetes, ulcer and stomach pain.

2. We have perused the affidavit filed in support of the petition seeking condonation of delay.

3. The petition is bereft of material particulars. There is no record to show the alleged illness of the petitioner. The alleged ailment is not so serious even to sign the papers. After all, there is no need for the physical presence of the appellant in the conduct of the appeal. What was required by him was to sign the vakalat and the affidavit along with memorandum of appeal and the remaining aspects would have been taken care by his counsel. More than three years have elapsed since passing of the preliminary decree. Now, yet another round of litigation will have to go in the form of final decree proceedings. Thus, we are not inclined to allow this petition. Accordingly, this petition stands dismissed. Consequently, the first appeal is dismissed at the S.R. stage.
